goal.en: Talk about jobs, study and money — including the verbs English insists on for each.
goal.ar: أن تتحدث عن العمل والدراسة والمال، مع الأفعال التي تصرّ الإنجليزية على استعمالها مع كل منها.

text.en: A job needs “a”: she is a nurse. Dropping it — “she is nurse” — is the single most common Arabic-speaker slip here, because Arabic needs no article.
text.ar: المهنة تأخذ a فنقول she is a nurse. وحذفها كما في she is nurse أشيع خطأ عند الناطقين بالعربية لأن العربية لا تحتاج أداة.

head: Word
Means
rows: the company or person who pays you
the person in charge of you

text.en: “Work” is uncountable: I have a lot of work. “Job” is countable: I have two jobs. “I have a work” is always wrong.
text.ar: كلمة work غير معدودة فنقول a lot of work، أما job فمعدودة فنقول two jobs. وجملة I have a work خطأ دائماً.

items.en: My sister is an engineer at a small company.
I work night shifts twice a week.

text.en: Study = the activity of reading and revising. Learn = the result, actually knowing it. You study for an exam so that you learn the material.
text.ar: study هو فعل المذاكرة نفسه، وlearn هي النتيجة أي أن تعرف المادة فعلاً. تذاكر study للامتحان لكي تتعلم learn المحتوى.

head: Verb
Goes with
rows: a mark, a grade, a degree

text.en: “I passed the exam” means you succeeded, not that you sat it. To say only that you attended it, use “I took the exam”.
text.ar: I passed the exam تعني «نجحت» لا «أدّيت». وللدلالة على مجرد الجلوس للامتحان قل I took the exam.

items.en: I studied all night and still failed.
items.ar: ذاكرت طوال الليل ومع ذلك رسبت.

items.en: She got a good mark in maths.
items.ar: حصلت على درجة جيدة في الرياضيات.

head: Verb
Pattern
Example
rows: I save a little each month.

text.en: Borrow means take; lend means give. «استعار» and «أعار» are two different verbs in Arabic too, so the trap is only which English word is which: you borrow FROM a person, you lend TO a person.
text.ar: borrow تعني «يستعير» وlend تعني «يُعير»، والفرق موجود في العربية أيضاً. المهم اتجاه الحرف: تستعير from شخص، وتُعير to شخص.

text.en: “Pay” takes “for” before the thing bought, but no “for” before the money or the person: I paid the driver 50 pounds for the ride.
text.ar: pay تأخذ for قبل الشيء المشترى، ولا تأخذها قبل المبلغ ولا قبل الشخص: I paid the driver 50 pounds for the ride.

explanation.en: Jobs take a/an in English even though Arabic needs no article.
explanation.ar: المهن تأخذ a أو an في الإنجليزية وإن كانت العربية لا تحتاج أداة.

options: I have a work tomorrow morning.
I have a lot of work tomorrow.
I have a job interview tomorrow.
I have two jobs at the moment.

explanation.en: Work is uncountable, so it cannot take “a”. Job is countable and can.
explanation.ar: كلمة work غير معدودة فلا تأخذ a، أما job فمعدودة وتأخذها.

prompt.en: The people you work with, at your own level, are your…
prompt.ar: من تعمل معهم في مستواك نفسه هم…

explanation.en: Colleagues work alongside you; an employer pays you.
explanation.ar: colleagues زملاء العمل، أما employer فهو رب العمل الذي يدفع لك.

prompt.en: Match the word to its meaning.

explanation.en: Employer and employee differ by two letters and mean opposite things — worth learning as a pair.
explanation.ar: employer وemployee يفترقان بحرفين ويحملان معنيين متقابلين، فاحفظهما معاً.

questions.sentence: I ___ for three hours last night.

explanation.en: The activity of working through material is “study”; “learn” is the result.
explanation.ar: فعل المذاكرة نفسه study، أما learn فهي النتيجة.

options: I passed the exam but I failed.
I took the exam but I failed.
I passed the exam, so I was happy.
I failed the exam and took it again.

explanation.en: “Passed” already means succeeded, so it cannot be followed by “failed”. The neutral verb is “took”.
explanation.ar: passed تعني «نجح» أصلاً فلا يصح أن يتبعها failed. الفعل المحايد هو took.

questions.sentence: You have to ___ your homework by Friday.

explanation.en: Hand in = give to a teacher. Hand out = distribute to many people.
explanation.ar: hand in تعني التسليم للمعلم، وhand out تعني التوزيع على كثيرين.

prompt.en: One word: to look at your notes again before an exam is to ___ (British English).
prompt.ar: كلمة واحدة: مراجعة الملاحظات قبل الامتحان في البريطانية تُسمّى ___

explanation.ar: revise البريطانية تقابل review الأمريكية، ولا تعني «يعدّل» في هذا السياق.

questions.sentence: I ___ fifty pounds on a new jacket.

explanation.en: Spend takes the money as its object: spend money on something.
explanation.ar: spend يأخذ المبلغ مفعولاً: spend money on something.

questions.sentence: Who ___ for the meal last night?

explanation.en: You pay FOR a thing. Spend needs an amount of money, not a meal.
explanation.ar: نقول pay for قبل الشيء، أما spend فتحتاج مبلغاً لا وجبة.

options: Can you borrow me your pen?
Can you lend me your pen?
I borrowed a pen from Sara.

explanation.en: You borrow from someone; you lend to someone. Here the speaker wants to receive, so the other person must lend.
explanation.ar: borrow تعني «يستعير» وlend تعني «يُعير». المتحدث هنا يريد أن يأخذ، فالفعل المطلوب من الآخر هو lend.

questions.sentence: The car is nice, but we can't ___ it this year.

explanation.en: Afford = have enough money for. It almost always appears with can or can't.
explanation.ar: afford تعني «يقدر مالياً»، وتأتي دائماً تقريباً مع can أو can't.

questions.answer: How much did the tickets cost

explanation.en: Cost takes the thing as subject: the tickets cost, not “you cost”.
explanation.ar: cost يجعل الشيء فاعلاً: the tickets cost لا you cost.

prompt.en: “I'm saving up for a laptop.” What is the speaker doing?
prompt.ar: ماذا يفعل المتحدث في هذه الجملة؟

options: Keeping money aside to buy it later.
Selling a laptop to get money.

explanation.en: Save up = collect money over time towards a specific purchase.
explanation.ar: save up تعني ادّخار المال تدريجياً لشراء شيء محدد.

questions.sentence: She ___ for the job last week and got an interview.

explanation.en: The fixed phrase is “apply for a job”. Ask and request take different objects.
explanation.ar: التعبير الثابت هو apply for a job، أما ask وrequest فتأخذان مفاعيل أخرى.
